title: Crew sizing, cost-tilt and pricing stress notebook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working sheet captures a compact set of headcount sizing alternatives + cost-tilt experiments for Q3–Q4 2026. The goal is to produce quick, actionable bundles the PLG and sales finance partners can sign off on within two weeks: 1) minimum runway-preserving crew sizes, 2) pricing/commitment levers that buy coverage, and 3) an operational tilt that shifts load between reserved and spot capacity to dampen unit cost shocks.

Executive note (TL;DR):
- Baseline: current committed headcount + reserved GPU purchase schedule consumes ~10.8M cash over next 12 months (incl 15% buffer).
- Target runways: Preserve 15 months -> need to cut ~18% nominal spend or offset with price/commit changes.
- Three prioritized levers: slow-hire freeze for non-critical roles (savings 6.2% run-rate), increase customer-facing price by 4% phased (recovers ~7% revenue), and implement capacity-tilt to 35% spot/65% reserved (saves ~3–4% infra cost).

Definitions and shorthand used below:
- Crew = active headcount (FTEs) excluding contractors.
- Cost-tilt = relative allocation between reserved capacity (Dedicated) and on-demand/spot (bursting).
- Spike buffer = short-term flexible fund to cover 4 weeks of peak traffic.
- Greenline, Lockstep, SurgeCushion = scenario names (detailed further down).

Current snapshot (inputs):
- Cash balance (2026-02-01): $62.5M
- Monthly burn (Feb 2026 baseline): $4.7M (S&M 35%, Eng 38%, G&A 15%, Infra 12%)
- Headcount (total FTEs): 152 (engineering 82, product/PM 10, DX/Docs 6, go-to-market 30, CS/Support 18, ops 6)

detailed_assumptions:
(1) Average fully loaded FTE cost = $190k/year. Contractors counted at 1.8x cost multiple when converted to FTE equivalent. (2) Reserved GPU mix saves 22% vs pure on-demand at current market assumptions; spot bursting saves 40% but has availability risk we model as 6% expected service degradation unless mitigated. (3) Revenue response elasticity: small PLG price increases show low churn initially; modeled revenue drop 0.6% per 1% price increase in Q1 after change, stabilizes by Q3. (4) Opex ramp: hiring leads to linear monthly spend after role start date + avg ramp 2 months to fully productive.

Quick math snippets (working):
- FTE save per hire freeze (14 hires) = 14 * 190k = $2.66M annualized -> ~22% of current burn reduction target.
- 4% price uplift across paid accounts (annualized revenue base $48M) = +$1.92M / year before churn; net conservatively +$1.6M after 18% elasticity loss profile.
- Capacity-tilt effect: baseline infra annual = $6.3M. Move to 35% spot reduces infra spend by ~3.6% (annual ~$227k). Combine with small quantization (model mix) saves additional ~$180k.

Operational execution checklist (short):
- Finance: finalize updated ARR model & re-run cohort LTVs (JIRA-FIN-412). Owner: Priya. Deadline: 2026-03-19.
- Product: identify list of non-productized features to de-prioritize (saves 0.8 FTE/quarter). Owner: Carlos. Deadline: 2026-03-12.
- Eng/Infra: implement staged spot pool + preempt fallback (SRE runbook v1). Owner: Ethan. Deadline: 2026-03-26.
- GTM: price change communication plan and trial exemptions for key enterprise customers. Owner: Sales Ops. Deadline: 2026-04-01.

Sensitivity matrix (short form):
- Price +4% (phased): Revenue net +3.3% (best), +1.0% (base conservative), -1.1% (worst with churn).
- Hire freeze efficacy: if voluntary attrition rises >8% during freeze then savings drop by 35% and replacement contractor pressure increases cost by 12%.
- Spot availability disruption: modeled as 6% service degradation -> triggers auto-fallback to reserved variants at 2x latency cost; effective infra savings then drop to ~1.0% instead of 3.6%.

Example micro-scenarios (single-line summaries):
- Greenline: slow hires, small product deferrals, maintain customer SLAs via reserved fallback. Net runway +2.4 months.
- Lockstep: small headcount trimming + price uplift + capacity tilt, prioritized to preserve growth posture. Net runway +3.8 months.
- SurgeCushion: preserve hiring, aggressive spot strategy, seek short-term debt (3 mo) to avoid layoffs; runway +0.6 months but preserves momentum.

Table: rough 12-month P&L modulation (annualized numbers, working):
- Baseline annualized spend: $56.4M
- Greenline spend: $52.8M (-6.4%)
- Lockstep spend: $50.6M (-10.2%) with +3.3% revenue tailwind
- SurgeCushion spend: $55.2M (-2.1%)

Risk register (prioritized):
1) Revenue churn risk from price change (mitigation: phased rollout + enterprise exemptions + credit).
2) Operational risk from spot unavailability (mitigation: canary spot pools + preempt fallback).
3) Morale risk from hiring freeze (mitigation: retention bonuses for critical ICs, re-evaluate in 6 weeks).
4) Timing risk for renewals (mitigation: reprice for upcoming renewals early).

Open questions for leadership: (a) acceptable minimum crew level for core infra ownership? (b) appetite for short-term debt vs small layoffs? (c) firm guardrails for enterprise exemptions to price increases?

Appendix: short run calculator paste (quick copy):
- Inputs: cash_balance, monthly_burn, avg_fte_cost, price_uplift_pct, spot_share_pct, hire_freeze_count
- Outputs: adjusted_runway_months, annual_savings, infra_saving_pct
Sample set: 62500000, 4700000, 190000, 0.04, 0.35, 14 -> adjusted_runway ~17.9 months (Lockstep)

References + links: CONFLUENCE-1082 (full ARR rework), JIRA-FIN-412 (sensitivity model), slack: #finance-runway (thread TS-123), github: github.com/redwood-inference/cost-tools/pr/87 (spot pool simulator).

Notes-to-self: keep this file lightweight; convert to canonical playbook only after one leadership sync. Expect to iterate with Sales Ops and Eng within 7–10 days.
